title: Concentration on an $L^1$-selected family
statement: Let $n,k\ge 0$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose $\varepsilon>0$. Assume the total squared Fourier weight of $f$ on sets of cardinality greater than $k$ is at most $\varepsilon/4$. Form the degree-at-most-$k$ Fourier truncation of $f$, and select the sets $S$ for which $(\varepsilon/4)\le \|\widehat{g}\|_1|\widehat{g}(S)|$, where $g$ is that truncation and $\|\widehat{g}\|_1$ is the sum of the absolute values of its Fourier coefficients. Then the total squared Fourier weight of $f$ outside the selected family is at most $\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: Fourier weight above degree $k$ is at most $\varepsilon/4$
